title: Your Amazing Heart
summary: How the heart pumps blood all around the body, every second of your life.

steps.title: A pump that never rests
sentences: Your heart is a muscle about the size of your fist.
It pumps blood around your body, beat after beat, day and night.
A child's heart beats roughly 70 to 100 times every minute when resting.
points: A muscle the size of a fist

steps.title: Two loops
sentences: The blood goes around in two loops.
One loop carries blood to the lungs to pick up oxygen.
The other loop carries that fresh blood to all parts of the body, and brings the used blood back.

steps.title: Four rooms
sentences: The heart has four rooms called chambers.
The two upper chambers are the atria and the two lower ones are the ventricles.
Little doors called valves make sure the blood only flows one way, and the 'lub-dub' sound you hear is those valves closing.

steps.title: Look after it
sentences: You can feel your pulse on your wrist, it is the blood pushing through with each heartbeat.
Running makes your heart beat faster because your muscles need more oxygen.
Playing, eating fruit and vegetables and sleeping well all help keep your heart strong.
points: Pulse = the push of each beat

facts: Your heart beats more than 100,000 times a day.
If all the blood vessels in an adult were laid end to end, they would stretch about 100,000 kilometres.
The blue whale has the biggest heart of any animal: one that was weighed came to about 180 kilograms.

quiz.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
quiz.why: Two atria and two ventricles make four chambers.

quiz.q: What do the valves of the heart do?
quiz.why: Valves are one-way doors for blood.

quiz.q: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
quiz.why: Working muscles need more oxygen, so the heart pumps faster to deliver it.

notes: Resting heart rate ranges are typical values and vary between children.
